units.zh: 龐統字士元，襄陽人也。
units.en: Pang Tong, whose courtesy name was Shiyuan, came from Xiangyang.
units.literal: Pang Tong, courtesy name Shiyuan, was a man of Xiangyang.

units.zh: 少時樸鈍，未有識者。
units.en: As a boy he seemed dull and unremarkable, and no one yet appreciated him.
units.literal: In youth he was plain and slow-witted; no one recognized his talent.

units.zh: 潁川司馬徽清雅有知人鑒，統弱冠往見徽，徽採桑於樹上，坐統在樹下，共語自晝至夜。
units.en: Sima Hui of Yingchuan was elegant and had a gift for sizing people up. When Tong came of age he paid him a visit: Hui was in a mulberry tree gathering leaves, had Tong sit below, and they conversed from dawn into the night.
units.literal: Sima Hui of Yingchuan was refined and discerning in judging men; when Tong reached his capped years he went to visit Hui. Hui was picking mulberries in a tree and seated Tong beneath the tree; they talked from day until night.

units.zh: 徽甚異之，稱統當南州士之冠冕，由是漸顯。
units.en: Hui found him remarkable and said Tong would stand first among the gentlemen of the south; thereafter Tong’s name slowly spread.
units.literal: Hui thought him extraordinary and declared that Tong would be the foremost scholar of the southern provinces; from this Tong gradually became known.

units.zh: 〈《襄陽記》曰：諸葛孔明為臥龍，龐士元為鳳雛，司馬德操為水鏡，皆龐德公語也。
units.en: 〈The Xiangyang Ji records that people called Zhuge Liang the Sleeping Dragon, Pang Tong the Fledgling Phoenix, and Sima Hui the Clear Mirror of Water—epithets attributed to Pang Degong.
units.literal: 〈The Xiangyang Ji says: Zhuge Kongming was called the Crouching Dragon, Pang Shiyuan the Young Phoenix, and Sima Decao the Water Mirror—all phrases of Lord Pang Degong.

units.zh: 德公，襄陽人。
units.en: Pang Degong was a native of Xiangyang.
units.literal: Degong was a man of Xiangyang.

units.zh: 孔明每至其家，獨拜床下，德公初不令止。
units.en: Whenever Zhuge Liang visited, he alone bowed low at the bedside; Degong did not at first tell him to rise.
units.literal: Whenever Kongming came to his house, he alone bowed at the foot of the bed; Degong at first did not tell him to stop.

units.zh: 德操嘗造德公，值其渡沔，上祀先人墓，德操徑入其室，呼德公妻子，使速作黍，「徐元直向雲有客當來就我與龐公譚。」
units.en: Once Sima Hui called on Degong while Degong was away—he had crossed the Han to tend his ancestors’ graves uphill. Hui walked straight in, told Degong’s wife and children to cook millet quickly, and said, “Xu Shu mentioned that a guest would come visit me and Master Pang.”
units.literal: Decao once went to visit Degong when Degong was crossing the Han to sacrifice at his ancestors’ tombs above; Decao went straight into his house, called to Degong’s wife and children, and had them hurry to prepare millet, saying, “Xu Yuanzhi said earlier that a guest would come to talk with me and Lord Pang.”

units.zh: 其妻子皆羅列拜於堂下，奔走供設。
units.en: The women lined up to bow in the hall below and bustled about laying out the meal.
units.literal: His wife and children all lined up and bowed in the hall below, rushing about to set out provisions.

units.zh: 須臾，德公還，直入相就，不知何者是客也。
units.en: Soon Degong came home, walked straight in, and sat down with everyone—no one could tell who was the guest.
units.literal: Presently Degong returned; he went straight in and joined them, not knowing which was the guest.

units.zh: 德操年小德公十歲，兄事之，呼作龐公，故世人遂謂龐公是德公名，非也。
units.en: Hui was ten years Degong’s junior yet honored him like an elder and called him “Lord Pang,” so folk mistook “Lord Pang” for Degong’s personal name—incorrectly.
units.literal: Decao was ten years younger than Degong but treated him as an elder brother and addressed him as Lord Pang; hence people in the world came to think “Lord Pang” was Degong’s name—it was not.

units.zh: 德公子山民，亦有令名，娶諸葛孔明小姊，為魏黃門吏部郎，早卒。
units.en: Degong’s son Shanmin likewise enjoyed a good name; he married Zhuge Liang’s elder sister and served Wei as a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Director of the Bureau of Appointments, but died young.
units.literal: Degong’s son Shanmin also had a fine reputation; he married Zhuge Kongming’s elder sister and served Wei as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and Director of the Bureau of Appointments; he died young.

units.zh: 子渙，字世文，晉太康中為牂牁太守。
units.en: His son Huan, courtesy name Shiwen, served as Administrator of Zangke during the Jin dynasty’s Taikang period.
units.literal: His son Huan, courtesy name Shiwen, became Administrator of Zangke in the Taikang era of Jin.

units.zh: 統，德公從子也，少未有識者，惟德公重之，年十八，使往見德操。
units.en: Tong was Degong’s nephew. As a youth none praised him except Degong; at eighteen Degong sent him to meet Sima Hui.
units.literal: Tong was Degong’s nephew; in youth no one recognized him—only Degong valued him. At eighteen Degong sent him to visit Decao.

units.zh: 德操與語，既而嘆曰：「德公誠知人，此實盛德也。」〉
units.en: After talking with him, Hui sighed, “Degong truly knows men—this is real moral discernment.”〉
units.literal: Decao spoke with him and afterward sighed, saying, “Degong truly knows how to judge men; this is indeed great virtue.”〉

units.zh: 後郡命為功曹。
units.en: The commandery later appointed him Clerk of Merit.
units.literal: Later the commandery appointed him Clerk of Merit.

units.zh: 性好人倫，勤於長養。
units.en: He delighted in appraising character and worked hard to mentor and lift others up.
units.literal: By nature he loved to discuss human relations and labored to nurture and promote others.

units.zh: 每所稱述，多過其才，時人怪而問之，統答曰：「當今天下大亂，雅道陵遲，善人少而惡人多。
units.en: When he praised people he often overstated their abilities; contemporaries asked why. Tong answered, “The empire is torn apart and civility is in ruins—the virtuous are scarce and the vicious plentiful.
units.literal: Whenever he praised someone, he often exceeded that person’s actual talents; people of the time wondered and asked him. Tong replied, “The realm is in great chaos; proper conduct has declined; good men are few and wicked many.

units.zh: 方欲興風俗，長道業，不美其譚即聲名不足慕企，不足慕企而為善者少矣。
units.en: I mean to revive decent habits and grow the moral vocation: unless people sound worthy in conversation, their reputations will not invite emulation—and without emulation few will choose the good.
units.literal: I wish to improve customs and advance the Way—if I do not praise their conversation, their fame will not be worth aspiring to; if fame is not worth aspiring to, few will strive to do good.

units.zh: 今拔十失五，猶得其半，而可以崇邁世教，使有志者自勵，不亦可乎？」
units.en: If I recommend ten and only five measure up, I still secure half the field and can thereby lift public teaching and stir the ambitious—is that not worthwhile?”
units.literal: Now if I promote ten and miss five, I still gain half, and can thereby elevate instruction for the age and spur those with ambition—may it not be acceptable?”

units.zh: 吳將周瑜助先主取荊州，因領南郡太守。
units.en: The Wu commander Zhou Yu helped Liu Bei secure Jingzhou and on that basis also served as Administrator of Nan Commandery.
units.literal: Wu general Zhou Yu aided the Former Lord in taking Jingzhou and therefore held concurrent office as Administrator of Nan Commandery.

units.zh: 瑜卒，統送喪至吳，吳人多聞其名。
units.en: When Zhou Yu died, Tong accompanied the bier east to Wu, where many had already heard of him.
units.literal: When Yu died, Tong escorted the funeral to Wu; many in Wu had heard his name.

units.zh: 及當西還，並會昌門，陸勣、顧劭、全琮皆往。
units.en: As he prepared to go west again, a gathering formed at Chang Gate: Lu Ji, Gu Shao, and Quan Cong all attended.
units.literal: When he was about to return west, they all met at Chang Gate—Lu Ji, Gu Shao, and Quan Cong all went.

units.zh: 統曰：「陸子可謂駑馬有逸足之力，顧子可謂駑牛能負重致遠也。」
units.en: Tong remarked, “Lu Ji is like a nag that still has a burst of speed; Gu Shao is like a draft ox that can haul a heavy load a long way.”
units.literal: Tong said, “Master Lu may be called a slow horse with the strength of a swift gallop; Master Gu may be called a slow ox able to bear heavy loads far.”

units.zh: 〈張勃吳錄曰：或問統曰：「如所目，陸子為勝乎？」
units.en: 〈Zhang Bo’s Record of Wu relates that someone asked Tong, “If that is so, does Lu Ji come out ahead?”
units.literal: 〈Zhang Bo’s Wu lu says: Someone asked Tong, “By that judgment, is Master Lu the better one?”

units.zh: 統曰：「駑馬雖精，所致一人耳。
units.en: Tong replied, “A nag may be spirited, yet what it carries is one rider.
units.literal: Tong said, “Though a slow horse may be keen, it carries only one person.

units.zh: 駑牛一日行三百里，所致豈一人之重哉！」
units.en: An ox plods three hundred li a day—what it hauls is far more than one man’s burden!”
units.literal: A slow ox travels three hundred li in a day—what it carries is surely not the weight of one man alone!”

units.zh: 劭就統宿，語，因問：「卿名知人，吾與卿孰愈？」
units.en: Gu Shao lodged with Tong that night and in conversation asked, “You are celebrated as a judge of men—which of us ranks higher?”
units.literal: Shao stayed overnight with Tong and conversed, then asked, “You are famed for knowing men—which of us two is better?”

units.zh: 統曰：「陶冶世俗，甄綜人物，吾不及卿；
units.en: Tong said, “In shaping popular esteem and cataloguing talent, I am not your match;
units.literal: Tong said, “In molding common opinion and surveying men, I am not your equal;

units.zh: 論帝王之秘策，攬倚伏之要最，吾似有一日之長。」
units.en: in weighing the hidden policies of emperors and the turning points of fortune and ruin, I believe I have the edge.”
units.literal: in discussing the secret strategies of emperors and kings and grasping the essentials of dependency and reversal, I seem to have the advantage for a day.”

units.zh: 劭安其言而親之。〉
units.en: Shao accepted this and grew intimate with him.〉
units.literal: Shao was satisfied with these words and drew close to him.〉

units.zh: 謂全琮曰：「卿好施慕名，有似汝南樊子昭。
units.en: To Quan Cong he said, “You are generous and crave a good name—you remind me of Fan Zizhao of Runan.
units.literal: To Quan Cong he said, “You love to give and seek renown—you resemble Fan Zizhao of Runan.

units.zh: 〈蔣濟《萬機論》雲許子將褒貶不平，以拔樊子昭而抑許文休。
units.en: 〈Jiang Ji’s Treatise on Myriad Affairs notes that Xu Shao’s praises and censures were skewed—he boosted Fan Zizhao and played down Xu Wenxiu.
units.literal: 〈Jiang Ji’s Wan ji lun says Xu Zijiang’s praise and blame were unfair—he elevated Fan Zizhao and belittled Xu Wenxiu.

units.zh: 劉曄曰：「子昭拔自賈豎，年至耳順，退能守靜，進能不苟。」
units.en: Liu Ye objected that Zizhao rose from a merchant family; at sixty he could still withdraw in calm or advance without bending principle.
units.literal: Liu Ye objected that Zizhao rose from a merchant’s son; at sixty he could retire in quiet when withdrawn and advance without compromise.

units.zh: 濟答曰：「子昭誠自長幼完潔，然觀其臿齒牙，樹頰胲，吐脣吻，自非文休敵也。」
units.en: Ji answered that Zizhao is modest and steady from youth to age, but look at those buck teeth, those jowls, that mouth—in looks he cannot rival Xu Wenxiu.
units.literal: Ji answered that Zizhao is indeed clean from youth to old age, yet look at his projecting teeth, his broad cheeks, his pursed lips—he is no match for Wenxiu.

units.zh: 胲音改。〉
units.en: The editorial note reads the syllable as gai.〉
units.literal: The gloss reads the syllable as gai.〉

units.zh: 雖智力不多，亦一時之佳也。」
units.en: His wit may be limited, yet he is still a notable man of the hour.”
units.literal: Though his intelligence is not great, he is still a fine man of his time.”

units.zh: 績、劭謂統曰：「使天下太平，當與卿共料四海之士。」
units.en: Lu Ji and Gu Shao told Tong, “Should the realm ever know peace, we would rank the talent of the four quarters at your side.”
units.literal: Ji and Shao said to Tong, “If the realm were at peace, we would survey the worthies of the four quarters with you.”

units.zh: 深與統相結而還。
units.en: They grew close to Tong and then took their leave.
units.literal: They formed a deep bond with Tong and returned.

units.zh: 先主領荊州，統以從事守耒陽令，在縣不治，免官。
units.en: While Liu Bei held Jingzhou, Tong served as Attendant and acting magistrate of Leiyang; his administration there was slack and he was removed from office.
units.literal: The Former Lord governed Jingzhou; Tong as Attendant served as magistrate of Leiyang and, while in the county, failed to govern well and was dismissed.

units.zh: 吳將魯肅遺先主書曰：「龐士元非百里才也，使處治中、別駕之任，始當展其驥足耳。」
units.en: Lu Su of Wu wrote Liu Bei, “Pang Tong is no petty county talent—give him an Administrator’s Assistant or Chief Clerk post and his stallion’s stride will finally show.”
units.literal: Wu general Lu Su wrote to the Former Lord, saying, “Pang Shiyuan is not talent for a hundred-li district; place him in the office of Administrator’s Assistant or Lieutenant Governor and only then will he stretch his thoroughbred’s legs.

units.zh: 諸葛亮亦言之於先主，先主見與善譚，大器之，以為治中從事。
units.en: Zhuge Liang spoke for him as well. Liu Bei received Tong, conversed at length, thought highly of him, and named him Assistant Clerk to the Administrator.
units.literal: Zhuge Liang also spoke of him to the Former Lord; the Former Lord met him and conversed well with him, greatly esteemed him, and appointed him Assistant in the Bureau of the Administrator.

units.zh: 〈江表傳曰：先主與統從容宴語，問曰：「卿為周公瑾功曹，孤到吳，聞此人密有白事，勸仲謀相留，有之乎？
units.en: 〈The Jiang Biao Zhuan states that Liu Bei banqueted with Tong and asked, “You were Zhou Yu’s Clerk of Merit. When I visited Wu I heard he secretly memorialized Sun Quan to keep me there—was that true?
units.literal: 〈Jiang biao zhuan says: The Former Lord spoke at leisure with Tong at a banquet and asked, “You served Zhou Gongjin as Clerk of Merit; when I came to Wu I heard this man secretly submitted a memorial urging Zhongmou to detain me—was it so?

units.zh: 在君為君，卿其無隱。」
units.en: A subject owes his liege plain speech—do not conceal anything.”
units.literal: For one’s lord one is loyal—hide nothing from me."

units.zh: 統對曰：「有之。」
units.en: Tong answered, “It happened.”
units.literal: Tong replied, “It was so.

units.zh: 備嘆息曰：「孤時危急，當有所求，故不得不往，殆不免周瑜之手！
units.en: Liu Bei sighed, “I was cornered and had to seek aid—I had to go and barely escaped Zhou Yu’s grasp!
units.literal: Bei sighed and said, “I was then in desperate straits and had to ask help—I had no choice but to go; I nearly fell into Zhou Yu’s hands!

units.zh: 天下智謀之士，所見略同耳。
units.en: Every keen mind in the land read the danger much the same way.
units.literal: The insightful strategists of the realm saw much the same.

units.zh: 時孔明諫孤莫行，其意獨篤，亦慮此也。
units.en: Zhuge Liang alone urged me not to travel—his concern ran deepest because he foresaw exactly this.
units.literal: At the time Kongming urged me not to go—his intent alone was earnest; he too feared this.

units.zh: 孤以仲謀所防在北，當賴孤為援，故決意不疑。
units.en: I believed Sun Quan’s defenses were directed northward and that he would need me as an ally, so I decided to go without hesitation.
units.literal: I thought Zhongmou’s concern was to the north and that he would rely on me as support—so I resolved without doubt.

units.zh: 此誠出於險塗，非萬全之計也。」〉
units.en: That was a gamble on a razor’s edge, no failsafe plan.”〉
units.literal: This truly meant walking a perilous path—not a plan of perfect safety.”〉

units.zh: 親待亞於諸葛亮，遂與亮併為軍師中郎將。
units.en: He honored Tong next after Zhuge Liang and made Tong and Liang joint Military Advisers of the Household.
units.literal: He treated him with intimacy second only to Zhuge Liang, and appointed Tong with Liang joint Military Advisers of the Household.

units.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：統說備曰：「荊州荒殘，人物殫盡，東有吳孫，北有曹氏，鼎足之計，難以得志。
units.en: 〈The Annals of the Nine Provinces records Tong urging Liu Bei: “Jingzhou is ruined and depopulated; Sun Quan bars you east and Cao Cao presses north—the three-way balance will be hard to achieve.
units.literal: 〈Jiu zhou chun qiu says: Tong urged Bei, saying, “Jingzhou is wasted and exhausted; its people are gone. East you have Sun of Wu, north you have the Cao clan—the tripod strategy will be hard to realize.

units.zh: 今益州國富民強，戶口百萬，四部兵馬，所出必具，寶貨無求於外，今可權藉以定大事。」
units.en: Yizhou is wealthy and strong—over a million households, four hosts ready for any campaign, goods produced at home. Seize it now as a temporary base and you can anchor the great enterprise.”
units.literal: Now Yizhou is rich and strong with a million households; its four armies can furnish whatever is needed; treasures need not be sought from outside—we may borrow it for the nonce to settle the great affair."

units.zh: 備曰：「今指與吾為水火者，曹操也，操以急，吾以寬；
units.en: Liu Bei replied, “My nemesis is Cao Cao: he drives men hard; I treat them gently;
units.literal: Bei said, “What stands against me like fire and water is Cao Cao—Cao is harsh, I am lenient;

units.zh: 操以暴，吾以仁；
units.en: he is cruel; I am humane;
units.literal: Cao is violent, I am benevolent;

units.zh: 操以譎，吾以忠；
units.en: he is treacherous; I am sincere;
units.literal: Cao is deceitful, I am loyal;

units.zh: 每與操反，事乃可成耳。
units.en: I set myself against him in every way—that is how success is won.
units.literal: In everything I oppose Cao—only then may affairs succeed.

units.zh: 今以小故而失信義於天下者，吾所不取也。」
units.en: To throw away good faith before the empire for a petty gain—I will not do it.”
units.literal: Now to lose trust and righteousness before the realm over a small matter—that I will not take."

units.zh: 統曰：「權變之時，固非一道所能定也。
units.en: Tong answered, “Fluid times are not mastered by a single rigid rule.
units.literal: Tong said, “In times of shifting circumstance, one path alone cannot settle things.

units.zh: 兼弱攻昧，五伯之事。
units.en: Annexing the feeble and striking the blind—that was the Five Hegemons’ business.
units.literal: To annex the weak and strike the dim—that was the way of the Five Hegemons.

units.zh: 逆取順守，報之以義，事定之後，封以大國，何負於信？
units.en: Take by surprise but govern afterward with virtue; reward justice with a generous fief—after victory, where is the broken pledge?
units.literal: To seize by force and rule by order, repay with righteousness—after the matter is settled, enfeoff with a large domain; where is the breach of trust?

units.zh: 今日不取，終為人利耳。」
units.en: Hesitate today and someone else will profit tomorrow.”
units.literal: If we do not take it today, in the end it will profit others."

units.zh: 備遂行。〉
units.en: Liu Bei followed his advice.〉
units.literal: Bei then proceeded.〉

units.zh: 亮留鎮荊州。
units.en: Zhuge Liang stayed behind to guard Jingzhou.
units.literal: Liang remained to guard Jingzhou.

units.zh: 統隨從入蜀。
units.en: Tong marched with him into Shu.
units.literal: Tong followed him into Shu.

units.zh: 益州牧劉璋與先主會涪，統進策曰：「今因此會，便可執之，則將軍無用兵之勞而坐定一州也。」
units.en: Yizhou Governor Liu Zhang feasted Liu Bei at Fu. Tong proposed: “Use this meeting to seize him—then you gain the province without a campaign.”
units.literal: Governor of Yizhou Liu Zhang met the Former Lord at Fu; Tong advanced a stratagem, saying, “Seize this occasion to arrest him, and you will take the province without the labor of arms.

units.zh: 先主曰：「初入他國，恩信未著，此不可也。」
units.en: Liu Bei refused: “I have only just entered his territory; my grace and credibility are not yet rooted—I cannot do this.”
units.literal: The Former Lord said, “I have just entered another’s land; my kindness and trust are not yet established—this cannot be done.

units.zh: 璋既還成都，先主當為璋北征漢中，統復說曰：「陰選精兵，晝夜兼道，徑襲成都；
units.en: After Liu Zhang went back to Chengdu, Liu Bei was to lead a northern expedition on Zhang’s behalf toward Hanzhong. Tong urged again: “Pick elite troops in secret, force-march day and night, and surprise Chengdu;
units.literal: After Zhang returned to Chengdu, the Former Lord was to campaign north for Zhang against Hanzhong; Tong again urged, saying, “Secretly select crack troops, march day and night by forced marches, and strike Chengdu by surprise;

units.zh: 璋既不武，又素無預備，大軍卒至，一舉便定，此上計也。
units.en: Zhang is no fighter and has left no defenses; strike once your army appears—this is the best plan.
units.literal: Zhang is neither martial nor long prepared; when your host arrives suddenly, one blow will settle it—this is the upper plan.

units.zh: 楊懷、高沛，璋之名將，各仗強兵，據守關頭，聞數有箋諫璋，使發遣將軍還荊州。
units.en: Yang Huai and Gao Pei are Liu Zhang’s chief captains, each with strong garrisons on the choke points; they have urged Zhang in repeated memorials to send you home to Jingzhou.
units.literal: Yang Huai and Gao Pei are Zhang’s famous generals; each commands strong troops and holds the passes; they have repeatedly sent letters urging Zhang to send you back to Jingzhou.

units.zh: 將軍未至，遣與相聞，說荊州有急，欲還救之，並使裝束，外作歸形；
units.en: Before you reach them, notify them that Jingzhou is in crisis and you must hurry back; pack your baggage and look as if you are leaving;
units.literal: Before you arrive, send word to them that Jingzhou is in urgent danger and you wish to return to rescue it—also order your baggage packed and outwardly show the appearance of departure;

units.zh: 此二子既服將軍英名，又喜將軍之去，計必乘輕騎來見，將軍因此執之，進取其兵，乃向成都，此中計也。
units.en: they admire your fame and will cheer your departure—they will ride out lightly to see you off; seize them, take their men, and swing toward Chengdu—the middle option.
units.literal: these two have long respected your renown and will rejoice at your going—they are sure to come on light horses to see you; seize them then, take their troops, and march on Chengdu—this is the middle plan.

units.zh: 退還白帝，連引荊州，徐還圖之，此下計也。
units.en: Fall back to Baidi, link arms with Jingzhou, and plot a slower return—the weakest plan.
units.literal: Withdraw to Baidi, link up with Jingzhou, and plan your return slowly—this is the lower plan.

units.zh: 若沈吟不去，將致大困，不可久矣。」
units.en: If you dawdle, you will land in deep trouble and cannot hold out long.”
units.literal: If you hesitate and do not go, you will fall into great distress—it cannot last long."

units.zh: 先主然其中計，即斬懷、沛，還向成都，所過輒克。
units.en: Liu Bei chose the middle course: he executed Huai and Pei and drove toward Chengdu, taking every place along the way.
units.literal: The Former Lord approved the middle plan: he executed Huai and Pei at once and marched back toward Chengdu, conquering wherever he passed.

units.zh: 於涪大會，置酒作樂，謂統曰：「今日之會，可謂樂矣。」
units.en: At Fu he threw a victory feast with wine and music and said to Tong, “This party is a fine celebration.”
units.literal: At Fu he held a great assembly, set out wine and music, and said to Tong, “Today’s gathering may truly be called joyous.

units.zh: 統曰：「伐人之國而以為歡，非仁者之兵也。」
units.en: Tong replied, “To conquer another’s country and call it mirth—that is not how a humane host behaves.”
units.literal: Tong said, “To attack another’s state and take it for celebration—this is not the army of a benevolent man.

units.zh: 先主醉，怒曰：「武王伐紂，前歌后舞，非仁者邪？
units.en: Drunk, Liu Bei flared: “King Wu punished Zhou while soldiers sang in front and danced behind—was that inhumane?
units.literal: The Former Lord, drunk, grew angry and said, “King Wu attacked Zhou—the front sang and the rear danced—was that not benevolent?

units.zh: 卿言不當，宜速起出！」
units.en: Your answer was rude—get out!”
units.literal: Your words are improper—leave at once!"

units.zh: 於是統逡巡引退。
units.en: Tong withdrew in confusion.
units.literal: Tong then drew back hesitantly.

units.zh: 先主尋悔，請還。
units.en: Liu Bei soon repented and summoned him back.
units.literal: The Former Lord soon regretted and asked him back.

units.zh: 統復故位，初不顧謝，飲食自若。
units.en: Tong took his old seat without apologizing and ate and drank as if nothing had happened.
units.literal: Tong resumed his former seat, offered no apology at all, and ate and drank as before.

units.zh: 先主謂曰：「向者之論，阿誰為失？」
units.en: Liu Bei asked, “In that exchange just now—who was wrong?”
units.literal: The Former Lord said, “In the debate just now—who was in the wrong?”

units.zh: 統對曰：「君臣俱失。」
units.en: Tong said, “Both lord and subject misstepped.”
units.literal: Tong replied, “Ruler and minister were both in the wrong.

units.zh: 先主大笑，宴樂如初。
units.en: Liu Bei laughed, and the banquet resumed as before.
units.literal: The Former Lord laughed aloud; the feast continued as before.

units.zh: 〈習鑿齒曰：夫霸王者，必體仁義以為本，仗信順以為宗，一物不具，則其道乖矣。
units.en: 〈Xi Zuochi writes: A true king roots himself in benevolence and duty and leans on sincerity and deference; lacking any piece, he loses the Way.
units.literal: 〈Xi Zuochi said: A hegemon-king must embody benevolence and righteousness as his foundation and rely on trust and obedience as his norm; if one thing is lacking, his Way is astray.

units.zh: 今劉備襲奪璋土，權以濟業，負信違情，德義俱愆，雖功由是隆，宜大傷其敗，譬斷手全軀，何樂之有？
units.en: Liu Bei grabbed Liu Zhang’s land by ruse to build his power—breaking faith and wronging kin, failing both virtue and obligation. Even if his fortunes rose, he should have smarted at the moral wound; it is like hacking off a limb to save the trunk—where is the delight?
units.literal: Now Liu Bei seized Liu Zhang’s territory by stratagem to accomplish his enterprise—he betrayed trust and violated right feeling; both virtue and duty failed. Though his success thereby rose, he ought to have ached at his moral defeat—it is like cutting off a hand to save the body; what joy is there?

units.zh: 龐統懼斯言之泄宣，知其君之必悟，故眾中匡其失，而不脩常謙之道，矯然太當，盡其蹇諤之風。
units.en: Pang Tong, lest blunt truth leak everywhere, knew his lord could still be corrected; before the assembly he checked Liu Bei’s excess—not with meek courtesy but with blunt protest worthy of a fearless counselor.
units.literal: Pang Tong feared such words would leak out; knowing his lord would surely see reason, in the crowd he corrected his fault—without observing ordinary modesty, abruptly too apt, displaying the manner of blunt remonstrance.

units.zh: 夫上失而能正，是有臣也，納勝而無執，是從理也；
units.en: When a sovereign’s fault can be amended, true ministers exist; when good advice wins without pride, reason prevails.
units.literal: When the ruler errs yet can be corrected, there are loyal ministers; when one accepts good counsel without stubbornness, one follows principle.

units.zh: 有臣則陛隆堂高，從理則群策畢舉；
units.en: Loyal ministers lift the throne; heeding principle lifts every policy.
units.literal: With ministers the hall rises high; following principle, every plan is raised.

units.zh: 一言而三善兼明，暫諫而義彰百代，可謂達乎大體矣。
units.en: One sentence reveals three virtues; one brave word beams across ages—this is seeing the whole picture.
units.literal: In one phrase three goods are made clear; in a moment’s remonstrance duty shines for a hundred generations—this may be called grasping the great frame.

units.zh: 若惜其小失而廢其大益，矜此過言，自絕遠讜，能成業濟務者，未之有也。
units.en: Clutch a petty slip and forfeit a great gain, or cling to prideful words and shut out far-sighted advice—no one who finished great work ever acted so.
units.literal: If one spares a small fault and abandons a great benefit, or prides oneself on that excessive speech and cuts oneself off from far counsel—none who could complete an enterprise and aid the task has ever done so.

units.zh: 臣松之以為謀襲劉璋，計雖出於統，然違義成功，本由詭道，心既內疚，則歡情自戢，故聞備稱樂之言，不覺率爾而對也。
units.en: Pei Songzhi argues: The stratagem against Liu Zhang did stem from Tong, but triumph bought through deceit leaves a guilty heart—joy cannot run free; hearing Liu Bei boast of mirth, Tong answered rashly.
units.literal: Pei Songzhi considers: The plan to surprise Liu Zhang did come from Tong, yet success contrary to duty arose from cunning; with guilt in the heart, gladness is naturally checked—hence when he heard Bei’s words about joy, he answered without thinking.

units.zh: 備宴酣失時，事同樂禍，自比武王，曾無愧色，此備有非而統無失，其雲「君臣俱失」，蓋分謗之言耳。
units.en: Liu Bei was drunk and spoke out of turn, almost gloating; likening himself to King Wu without shame—there the lord erred, not the minister. Calling both “wrong” merely spread blame.
units.literal: Bei was drunk and mistimed, his conduct like rejoicing in disaster; comparing himself to King Wu without shame—here Bei was wrong and Tong was not; to say “ruler and minister were both wrong” was words to share blame.

units.zh: 習氏所論，雖大旨無乖，然推演之辭，近為流宕也。〉
units.en: Xi’s essay hits the broad point yet its elaboration wanders into flourish.
units.literal: Xi’s discussion, though its main thrust is not astray, verges on excessive rhetoric in the elaboration.

units.zh: 進圍雒縣，統率眾攻城，為流矢所中，卒，時年三十六。
units.en: When the army advanced to invest Luoxian, Tong led the assault and was hit by a stray arrow; he died at thirty-six.
units.literal: Advancing to besiege Luoxian, Tong led the host to assault the city; he was struck by a stray arrow and died; he was thirty-six.

units.zh: 先主痛惜，言則流涕。
units.en: Liu Bei mourned deeply and wept whenever Tong’s name arose.
units.literal: The Former Lord grieved bitterly; whenever he spoke of it he wept.

units.zh: 拜統父議郎，遷諫議大夫，諸葛亮親為之拜。
units.en: He ennobled Tong’s father as a Court Gentleman and advanced him to Grand Counselor of the Household; Zhuge Liang himself led the ceremony of respect.
units.literal: Tong’s father was appointed Court Gentleman; he was promoted to Grand Counselor of the Household; Zhuge Liang personally performed the obeisance for him.

units.zh: 追賜統爵關內侯，諡曰靖侯。
units.en: Tong was posthumously invested as a secondary marquis (Marquis Within the Passes) with the posthumous name “Jing” (Stern).
units.literal: Tong was posthumously enfeoffed with rank as Marquis Within the Passes and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

units.zh: 統子宏，字巨師，剛簡有臧否，輕傲尚書令陳袛，為袛所抑，卒於涪陵太守。
units.en: Tong’s son Hong, courtesy name Jushi, spoke plainly in praise and blame; he looked down on Palace Secretariat Director Chen Zhi, who retaliated; Hong ended his career as Administrator of Fuling.
units.literal: Tong’s son Hong, courtesy name Jushi, was blunt and direct in praising and blaming; he slighted Director of the Secretariat Chen Zhi and was checked by Zhi; he died as Administrator of Fuling.

units.zh: 統弟林，以荊州治中從事參鎮北將軍黃權征吳，值軍敗，隨權入魏，魏封列侯，至鉅鹿太守。
units.en: Pang Tong’s brother Lin served as an assistant in Jingzhou’s administration under General Who Guards the North Huang Quan on the Wu expedition; after the rout he followed Huang Quan into Wei, received a full marquisate from Wei, and eventually governed Julu as prefect.
units.literal: Tong's younger brother Lin, as Assistant in the Bureau of the Administrator of Jingzhou, accompanied General Who Guards the North Huang Quan on the campaign against Wu; when the army was defeated he followed Quan into Wei; Wei enfeoffed him as a full marquis, and he rose to Administrator of Julu.

units.zh: 〈《襄陽記》曰：林婦，同郡習禎妺。
units.en: 〈According to the Xiangyang Ji, Lin married Xi Zhen’s younger sister, a woman from the same district.
units.literal: 〈The Xiangyang Ji says: Lin’s wife was the younger sister of Xi Zhen of the same commandery.

units.zh: 禎事在楊戲《輔臣贊》。
units.en: Xi Zhen’s biography appears in Yang Xi’s Ministerial Encomia.
units.literal: Zhen's career is treated in Yang Xi's Eulogies to Ministers.

units.zh: 曹公之破荊州，林婦與林分隔，守養弱女十有餘年，後林隨黃權降魏，始復集聚。
units.en: After Cao Cao seized Jingzhou, Lin’s wife lived apart from him for over a decade, raising their young daughter alone; once Lin crossed to Wei with Huang Quan, husband and wife were finally reunited.
units.literal: When the Duke of Cao took Jingzhou, Lin’s wife was separated from Lin; for more than ten years she kept and raised a young daughter; only after Lin followed Huang Quan in surrender to Wei did they reunite.

units.zh: 魏文帝聞而賢之，賜床帳衣服，以顯其義節。〉
units.en: Cao Pi heard the story, admired her virtue, and rewarded her with bedding and clothing to honor her steadfast conduct.〉
units.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei heard of this and deemed her worthy; he bestowed bed curtains and garments to display her righteousness.〉

units.zh: 法正字孝直，
units.en: Fa Zheng—courtesy name Xiaozhi—
units.literal: Fa Zheng, courtesy name Xiaozhi,

units.en: Editor’s mark: right column.
units.literal: (right-hand column).

units.zh: 扶風郿人也。
units.en: He was a native of Mei in Fufeng Commandery.
units.literal: He was a man of Mei in Fufeng.

units.zh: 祖父真，有清節高名。
units.en: His grandfather Zhen enjoyed renown for purity of character.
units.literal: His grandfather Zhen had unsullied integrity and a lofty reputation.

units.zh: 〈三輔決錄注曰：真字高卿，少明五經，兼通讖緯，學無常師，名有高才。
units.en: 〈The gloss on the Sanfu jue lu records that Zhen, style Gaoqing, mastered the Five Classics in youth and probed prognostic texts as well; though without a regular tutor, he was celebrated as gifted.
units.literal: 〈The Commentary on the Sanfu jue lu says: Zhen, courtesy name Gaoqing, in youth mastered the Five Classics and also understood prophecy and apocrypha; he had no fixed teacher but was famed for outstanding talent.

units.zh: 常幅巾見扶風守，守曰：「哀公雖不肖，猶臣仲尼，柳下惠不去父母之邦，欲相屈為功曹何如？」
units.en: He presented himself informally to the prefect of Fufeng, who urged him: “Even a flawed lord like Duke Ai retained Confucius; Liuxia Hui refused to abandon his homeland—might you accept appointment as Clerk of Merit?”
units.literal: He usually wore a plain scholar’s headcloth to meet the Administrator of Fufeng, who said: “Though Duke Ai was unworthy, he still had Confucius as his minister; Liuxia Hui would not leave his parents’ state—I wish to press you to take office as Clerk of Merit—what say you?”

units.zh: 真曰：「以明府見待有禮，故四時朝覲，若欲吏使之，真將在北山之北南山之南矣。」
units.en: Zhen answered: “You honor me with courtesy, so I visit each season; force me into office and I shall vanish beyond the northern hills or the southern ranges.”
units.literal: Zhen replied: “Because my lord treats me courteously, I pay seasonal visits; if you insist on binding me to clerical duty, you will find me north of North Mountain or south of South Mountain.”

units.zh: 扶風守遂不敢以為吏。
units.en: The prefect dropped the matter and stopped pressing him.
units.literal: The Administrator of Fufeng then dared not press him into service.

units.zh: 初，真年未弱冠，父在南郡，步往候父，已欲去，父留之待正旦，使觀朝吏會。
units.en: Once, before Zhen came of age, his father was stationed in Nan Commandery; he walked there to see him, prepared to depart, but his father kept him through New Year’s morning to watch the clerks’ gathering.
units.literal: At first, before Zhen reached his capped years, his father was in Nan Commandery; he walked thither to visit his father and was about to leave when his father detained him for New Year’s Day and had him observe the assembly of court clerks.

units.zh: 會者數百人，真於窗中闚其與父語。
units.en: Hundreds were present; Zhen watched from behind a lattice as they spoke with his father.
units.literal: Several hundred attended; Zhen peeked from a window at their conversation with his father.

units.zh: 畢，問真「孰賢」？
units.en: Afterward he asked Zhen, “Who stands out among them?”
units.literal: When it ended, he asked Zhen, “Which man is the worthier?”

units.zh: 真曰：「曹掾胡廣有公卿之量。」
units.en: Zhen replied: “Hu Guang of the clerks has the makings of a high minister.”
units.literal: Zhen said: “Assistant Clerk Hu Guang has the stature of a minister or excellency.”

units.zh: 其後廣果歷九卿三公之位，世以服真之知人。
units.en: Hu Guang later climbed through the Nine Ministers to the Three Excellencies, and contemporaries marveled at Zhen’s eye for talent.
units.literal: Later Hu Guang indeed rose through the Nine Ministers and Three Excellencies; the age admired Zhen’s judgment of men.

units.zh: 前後徵辟，皆不就，友人郭正等美之，號曰玄德先生。
units.en: He refused every summons; companions like Guo Zheng lauded him and dubbed him Master Xuande.
units.literal: Summoned repeatedly to office, he declined each time; friends such as Guo Zheng praised him and styled him Master Xuande.

units.zh: 年八十九，中平五年卒。
units.en: He passed away at eighty-nine in Zhongping 5.
units.literal: He died at eighty-nine in the fifth year of Zhongping.

units.zh: 正父衍，字季謀，司徒掾、廷尉左監。〉
units.en: Fa Zheng’s father Yan, courtesy Jimou, served as an aide to the Minister over the Masses and as Left Overseer under the Minister of Justice.〉
units.literal: Zheng's father Yan, courtesy name Jimou, was an aide to the Minister of Education and Left Overseer of the Court.〉

units.zh: 建安初，天下饑荒，正與同郡孟達俱入蜀依劉璋，久之為新都令，後召署軍議校尉。
units.en: Early in Jian’an, famine drove Fa Zheng and fellow townsman Meng Da into Shu under Liu Zhang; years later he became magistrate of Xindu, then acting Colonel for Military Deliberation.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jian’an era the realm was starving; Zheng and Meng Da of the same commandery both entered Shu to rely on Liu Zhang; after a long interval he became magistrate of Xindu, then was summoned and appointed Colonel Who Discusses the Army.

units.zh: 既不任用，又為其州邑俱僑客者所謗無行，志意不得。
units.en: Passed over for higher posts and maligned by other outsiders in the province as dissolute, he grew frustrated and idle.
units.literal: Since he was not promoted and was slandered as worthless by fellow sojourners from town and province alike, his ambitions found no outlet.

units.zh: 益州別駕張松與正相善，忖璋不足與有為，常竊嘆息。
units.en: Provincial Lieutenant Governor Zhang Song befriended Fa Zheng; both concluded Liu Zhang could achieve nothing grand, and Song often groaned in private.
units.literal: Lieutenant Governor Zhang Song was intimate with Zheng; reckoning Liu Zhang incapable of great deeds, he often sighed in secret.

units.zh: 松於荊州見曹公還，勸璋絕曹公而自結先主。
units.en: After Song returned from meeting Cao Cao in Jingzhou, he urged Liu Zhang to renounce Cao and ally with Liu Bei.
units.literal: Song, returning from seeing the Duke of Cao in Jingzhou, urged Liu Zhang to break with Cao and align with the Former Lord.

units.zh: 璋曰：「誰可使者？」
units.en: Liu Zhang asked, “Who is fit to go?”
units.literal: Liu Zhang said: “Whom can we send?”

units.zh: 松乃舉正，正辭讓，不得已而往。
units.en: Song recommended Fa Zheng, who protested yet finally obeyed.
units.literal: Song then nominated Zheng; Zheng declined but had no choice but to go.

units.zh: 正既還，為松稱說先主有雄略，密謀協規，原共戴奉，而未有緣。
units.en: Back in Shu, Fa Zheng praised Liu Bei’s strategic vision to Song; the two conspired quietly to enthrone him but could find no occasion.
units.literal: When Zheng returned, he told Song that the Former Lord possessed heroic designs; they secretly plotted in concert and wished to serve him together but lacked an opening.

units.zh: 後因璋聞曹公欲遣將征張魯之有懼心也，松遂說璋宜迎先主，使之討魯，復令正銜命。
units.en: When Liu Zhang heard Cao Cao might march on Zhang Lu and began to panic, Song argued for inviting Liu Bei to attack Zhang Lu and sent Fa Zheng once more with the summons.
units.literal: Later, because Liu Zhang learned that the Duke of Cao planned to send generals against Zhang Lu and grew fearful, Song persuaded Liu Zhang to welcome the Former Lord and dispatch him against Lu, and again ordered Zheng to bear the commission.

units.zh: 正既宣旨，陰獻策於先主曰：「以明將軍之英才，乘劉牧之懦弱；
units.en: Once Fa Zheng delivered the edict, he whispered to Liu Bei: “Given your gifts as commander and Liu Zhang’s weakness,
units.literal: After Zheng had proclaimed the decree, he secretly urged the Former Lord: “With your brilliance, Brilliant General, and Liu the Governor’s timidity;

units.zh: 張松，州之股肱，以響應於內；
units.en: with Zhang Song—the provincial pillar—to rise inside in answer,
units.literal: Zhang Song, the province’s chief prop, to echo you within;

units.zh: 然後資益州之殷富，馮天府之險阻，以此成業，猶反掌也。」
units.en: you can exploit Yizhou’s wealth and its natural fortress—victory will come like flipping your palm.”
units.literal: then drawing on Yizhou’s abundance and leaning on heaven’s barriers, you may seize dominion as easily as turning your hand.”

units.zh: 先主然之，溯江而西，與璋會涪。
units.en: Liu Bei accepted the plan, sailed west along the Yangzi, and joined Liu Zhang at Fu.
units.literal: The Former Lord agreed; he went upriver west and met Liu Zhang at Fu.

units.zh: 北至葭萌，南還取璋。
units.en: He pushed north to Jiameng, then doubled back south to overpower Liu Zhang.
units.literal: He advanced north to Jiameng, then wheeled south to seize Liu Zhang.

units.zh: 鄭度說璋曰：
units.en: Zheng Du counseled Liu Zhang:
units.literal: Zheng Du urged Liu Zhang:

units.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：度，廣漢人，為州從事。〉
units.en: 〈The Chronicles of Huayang records that Du was from Guanghan and served as a provincial attendant.〉
units.literal: 〈The Huayang guo zhi says: Du was a man of Guanghan and served as provincial Attendant.〉

units.zh: 「左將軍縣軍襲我，兵不滿萬，士眾未附，野谷是資，軍無輜重。
units.en: “The General of the Left attacks us with a stranded force—under ten thousand men, loyalty still unsettled, living off the countryside, no supply wagons behind him.
units.literal: “General of the Left leads an isolated army against me—fewer than ten thousand men, the troops not yet attached to him, subsisting on wild grain, with no baggage train.

units.zh: 其計莫若盡驅巴西、梓潼民內涪水以西，其倉廩野谷，一皆燒除，高壘深溝，靜以待之。
units.en: Your best move is to relocate Baxi and Zitong populations west of the Fu, burn every store of grain, fortify walls and ditches, and stand fast.
units.literal: Nothing beats driving every household of Baxi and Zitong west of the Fu River, burning all granaries and field grain, raising high ramparts and digging deep moats, and waiting in silence.

units.zh: 彼至，請戰，勿許，久無所資，不過百日，必將自走。
units.en: When they ask to fight, deny them; starved within months they will break.
units.literal: When they arrive and beg battle, refuse; long bereft of supplies, within a hundred days they will scatter of themselves.

units.zh: 走而擊之，則必禽耳。」
units.en: Hit them on the run and they are yours.”
units.literal: Strike them in retreat and you will surely take them captive.”

units.zh: 先主聞而惡之，以問正。
units.en: Liu Bei heard the scheme with dread and questioned Fa Zheng.
units.literal: The Former Lord heard this with alarm and consulted Zheng.

units.zh: 正曰：「終不能用，無可憂也。」
units.en: Fa Zheng replied: “Liu Zhang will never use it—you need not worry.”
units.literal: Zheng said: “He will never adopt it—there is nothing to fear.”

units.zh: 璋果如正言，謂其群下曰：「吾聞拒敵以安民，未聞動民以避敵也。」
units.en: Liu Zhang behaved exactly as Fa Zheng foretold, declaring to his staff: “We resist foes to protect the people—not to harrow the people for fear of foes.”
units.literal: Liu Zhang indeed acted as Zheng predicted, telling his officers: “I have heard of beating the enemy to bring peace to the people; I have never heard of disturbing the people to dodge the enemy.”

units.zh: 於是黜度，不用其計。
units.en: He cashiered Zheng Du and set the stratagem aside.
units.literal: Thereupon he dismissed Du and rejected his plan.

units.zh: 及軍圍雒城，正箋與璋曰：
units.en: During the siege of Luocheng, Fa Zheng sent Liu Zhang a letter:
units.literal: When the army besieged Luocheng, Zheng wrote Liu Zhang:

units.zh: 正受性無術，盟好違損，懼左右不明本末，必並歸咎，蒙恥沒身，辱及執事，是以損身於外，不敢反命。
units.en: I am no schemer; the covenant between us broke—I worry your attendants misunderstand the tale and will blame us together; I would die shamed and stain your name, so I remain outside and cannot answer your summons.
units.literal: By temperament I lack craft; our sworn friendship was violated and harmed—I fear those at your side do not grasp the whole story and will heap blame together; I would wear shame to the grave and disgrace your office—therefore I hazard myself abroad and dare not face you with a report.

units.zh: 恐聖聽穢惡其聲，故中間不有箋敬，顧念宿遇，瞻望悢々。
units.en: I stayed silent lest my voice disgust your ears, yet I recall our past ties and look toward you with sorrow.
units.literal: I feared your sacred hearing would loathe the sound, hence between times I sent no respectful letters; still I remember our old meeting and gaze afar with aching regret.

units.zh: 然惟前後披露腹心，自從始初以至於終，實不藏情，有所不盡，但愚闇策薄，精誠不感，以致於此耳。
units.en: From beginning to end I held nothing back; my stupidity and thin counsel failed to touch you—that is how we came here.
units.literal: Yet I have laid bare my heart before and after—from first to last I hid no true feeling; what was lacking was only my dull wit and shallow schemes; my sincerity did not move you, and events reached this pass.

units.zh: 今國事已危，禍害在速，雖捐放於外，言足憎尤，猶貪極所懷，以盡餘忠。
units.en: The realm totters; ruin nears. Though exile makes my counsel odious, I speak my utmost to prove fealty.
units.literal: Now the state’s peril is urgent; disaster strikes swiftly—though cast off abroad and my words liable to hatred, I still pour out what I hold to exhaust my remaining loyalty.

units.zh: 明將軍本心，正之所知也，實為區區不欲失左將軍之意，而卒至於是者，左右不達英雄從事之道，謂可違信黷誓，而以意氣相致，日月相遷，趨求順耳悅目，隨阿遂指，不圖遠慮為國深計故也。
units.en: I understand your heart—you meant no slight to Liu Bei, yet courtiers mistook hero-to-hero dealings: they imagined oaths disposable, traded smooth praise season by season, chased flattery, and never planned for the realm.
units.literal: Your own intent, Brilliant General, I know well—I truly wished only not to wound General of the Left’s feelings, yet we arrived here because those about you did not grasp how heroes serve one another: they thought sworn faith could be broken on a whim, exchanging pleasant flattery day by day, chasing agreeable words and looks, currying favor without thinking far ahead for the state.

units.zh: 事變既成，又不量強弱之勢，以為左將軍縣遠之眾，糧谷無儲，欲得以多擊少，曠日相持。
units.en: After the rupture they still misread power—thinking Liu Bei’s distant army had no grain and could be overwhelmed by mass and delay.
units.literal: Once matters turned, they again misjudged strength: they supposed General of the Left’s distant troops lacked grain and hoped superior numbers in a long stalemate would prevail.

units.zh: 而從關至此，所歷輒破，離宮別屯，日自零落。
units.en: Yet from the frontier to here each strongpoint has collapsed; outposts dwindle by the day.
units.literal: Yet from the passes hither every position has fallen; detached camps crumble daily.

units.zh: 雒下雖有萬兵，皆壞陳之卒，破軍之將，若欲爭一旦之戰，則兵將勢力，實不相當。
units.en: The garrison below Luoxia may count ten thousand, but they are shattered units led by beaten generals; a single pitched battle cannot balance the odds.
units.literal: Though Luoxia holds ten thousand men, they are broken formations and defeated captains—if you wager everything on one clash, arms and commanders no longer match.

units.zh: 各欲遠期計糧者，今此營守已固，谷米已積，而明將軍土地日削，百姓日困，敵對遂多，所供遠曠。
units.en: Anyone banking on prolonged logistics should note: our lines are set and granaries full, while your domain shrinks, your people weaken, foes crowd about, and convoys from afar cannot feed you.
units.literal: Those counting on distant grain must see: our camps are firm now, stores piled high, while your territory shrinks daily, the people wear thin, enemies multiply, and distant supplies cannot reach you.

units.zh: 愚意計之，謂必先竭，將不復以持久也。
units.en: By my poor judgment you will fail before we do—you cannot outlast us.
units.literal: In my humble reckoning you must exhaust yourselves first—you cannot endure a war of attrition.

units.zh: 空爾相守，猶不相堪，今張益德數萬之眾，已定巴東，入犍為界，分平資中、德陽，三邈道侵，將何以御之？
units.en: Sheer standoff would exhaust you; now Zhang Fei commands myriad troops holding Badong, advancing through Qianwei, dividing Zizhong and Deyang, pressing on three axes—how can you stop him?
units.literal: Idle stalemate alone would strain you; now Zhang Yide leads tens of thousands who have secured Badong, pushed into Qianwei, split Zizhong and Deyang, and threaten along three roads—how will you resist?

units.zh: 本為明將軍計者，必謂此軍縣遠無糧，饋運不及，兵少無繼。
units.en: Your advisers assumed Liu Bei’s army was isolated, unfed, outnumbered, unreinforced.
units.literal: Those who plotted for you surely assumed this army was far from home without grain, supplies unable to catch up, soldiers few and reinforcements none.

units.zh: 今荊州道通，眾數十倍，加孫車騎遣弟及李異、甘寧等為其後繼。
units.en: But Jingzhou’s road runs clear; our host multiplies yours many times; Sun Quan’s brother with Li Yi, Gan Ning, and more marches in support.
units.literal: Now the Jingzhou route is open; our numbers exceed yours tenfold, and General of Chariots and Cavalry Sun’s younger brother with Li Yi, Gan Ning, and others follow as a second wave.

units.zh: 若爭客主之勢，以土地相勝者，今此全有巴東，廣漢、犍為，過半已定，巴西一郡，復非明將軍之有也。
units.en: Measured by territory we already own Badong outright, most of Guanghan and Qianwei, and Baxi can no longer be called yours.
units.literal: If you contest host and guest by land, today we wholly hold Badong and more than half of Guanghan and Qianwei—nor does Baxi alone remain yours.

units.zh: 計益州所仰惟蜀，蜀亦破壞；
units.en: The province depends on the Shu heartland, yet that core is ruined;
units.literal: Yizhou relies on Shu command for sustenance, yet Shu itself lies broken;

units.zh: 三分亡二，吏民疲睏，思為亂者十戶而八；
units.en: two-thirds gone; officials and peasants stagger—eight houses in ten simmer for rebellion.
units.literal: two parts in three are lost; officials and commoners stagger with fatigue—eight households in ten ache for revolt.

units.zh: 若敵遠則百姓不能堪役，敵近則一旦易主矣。
units.en: Keep the enemy far and corvée breaks the people; draw him close and masters swap in a day.
units.literal: If the foe stays distant the people cannot bear corvée; if the foe draws near authority changes overnight.

units.zh: 廣漢諸縣，是明比也。
units.en: Guanghan’s towns prove it plainly.
units.literal: The counties of Guanghan are plain proof.

units.zh: 又魚復與關頭實為益州福禍之門，今二門悉開，堅城皆下，諸軍並破，兵將俱盡，而敵家數道併進，已入心腹，坐守都、雒，存亡之勢，昭然可見。
units.en: Yufu and the frontier passes are Yizhou’s hinge of weal and woe—both lie open now; cities fell, hosts ruined. Enemy columns pierce your bowels; guarding only Chengdu and Luoxia leaves fate starkly clear.
units.literal: Moreover Yufu and the passes are truly Yizhou’s gates of fortune and ruin—now both stand open, every fortress reduced, armies shattered and leaders gone, while foes advance on many roads deep into your vitals; sitting guard over Chengdu and Luoxia, survival hangs before your eyes.

units.zh: 斯乃大略，其外較耳，其餘屈曲，難以辭極也。
units.en: That is the shape of it; finer points exceed speech.
units.literal: This is the broad outline—the rest is detail beyond words.

units.zh: 以正下愚，猶知此事不可覆成，況明將軍左右明智用謀之士，豈當不見此數哉？
units.en: Even a dullard like me sees restoration is impossible—can your clever ministers miss the tally?
units.literal: Though I am bottom foolish, even I know this cannot be repaired—how could your wise counselors beside you fail to see these figures?

units.zh: 旦夕偷幸，求容取媚，不慮遠圖，莫肯盡心獻良計耳。
units.en: They cling to lucky survival, angling for smiles, never plotting ahead—none offers honest counsel.
units.literal: Day and night they cling to luck, flattering for favor, never weighing distant plans—none will lay out a loyal stratagem.

units.zh: 若事窮勢迫，將各索生，求濟門戶，展轉反覆，與今計異，不為明將軍盡死難也。
units.en: Pressed tight they will seize safety, barter loyalties, flip sides—nothing like their present advice—and will not perish for your cause.
units.literal: If cornered they will each chase survival, shift allegiance to save their houses, reverse course—far from today’s counsel—and will not die for you, Brilliant General.

units.zh: 而尊門猶當受其憂。
units.en: Your clan will still suffer the grief.
units.literal: Yet your noble house will still bear the grief.

units.zh: 正雖獲不忠之謗，然心自謂不負聖德，顧惟分義，實竊痛心。
units.en: Men call me traitor, yet I feel I have not wronged your kindness; weighing obligation, my heart breaks.
units.literal: Though I bear the slander of disloyalty, in my heart I believe I have not betrayed your grace; weighing duty and bond, I ache in secret.

units.zh: 左將軍從本舉來，舊心依依，實無薄意。
units.en: Liu Bei answered your first call; his affection remains—he bore you no ill will.
units.literal: General of the Left came at your original summons; his old goodwill endures—he never meant slight.

units.zh: 愚以為可圖變化，以保尊門。
units.en: I still think accommodation can shield your house.
units.literal: I believe terms may yet change to preserve your noble line.

units.zh: 十九年，進圍成都，璋蜀郡太守許靖將逾城降，事覺，不果。
units.en: In year 19 the army closed on Chengdu; Xu Jing, prefect of Shu under Liu Zhang, tried to slip over the wall to defect but was caught and could not complete it.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year they advanced to besiege Chengdu; Xu Jing, Liu Zhang’s Administrator of Shu Commandery, attempted to climb the walls and surrender but was discovered and failed.

units.zh: 璋以危亡在近，故不誅靖。
units.en: With collapse imminent Liu Zhang spared Xu Jing’s life.
units.literal: Because ruin pressed near, Liu Zhang did not execute Xu Jing.

units.zh: 璋既稽服，先主以此薄靖不用也。
units.en: Once Liu Zhang capitulated, Liu Bei despised Xu Jing and hesitated to use him.
units.literal: After Liu Zhang submitted, the Former Lord thought little of Xu Jing and would not employ him.

units.zh: 正說曰：「天下有獲虛譽而無其實者，許靖是也。
units.en: Fa Zheng argued: “The world holds reputations without substance—Xu Jing is one.
units.literal: Zheng urged: “The realm has men who win empty fame without substance—Xu Jing is such.

units.zh: 然今主公始創大業，天下之人不可戶說，靖之浮稱，播流四海，若其不禮，天下之人以是謂主公為賤賢也。
units.en: Yet as you launch your rule you cannot lecture every home; Xu Jing’s renown rings everywhere—if you dishonor him, people will call you contemptuous of talent.
units.literal: Yet now you inaugurate a great enterprise; you cannot explain yourself household by household—Xu Jing’s inflated name circulates the realm—if you slight him, folk will say you scorn worthies.

units.zh: 宜加敬重，以眩遠近，追昔燕王之待郭隗。」
units.en: Elevate him to impress distant audiences, as King Zhao of Yan honored Guo Wei.”
units.literal: Honor him to dazzle near and far, emulating the King of Yan’s treatment of Guo Wei.”

units.zh: 先主於是乃厚待靖。
units.en: Liu Bei accordingly welcomed Xu Jing with honor.
units.literal: The Former Lord then treated Xu Jing generously.

units.zh: 〈孫盛曰：夫禮賢崇德，為邦之要道，封墓式閭，先王之令軌，故必以體行英邈，高義蓋世，然後可以延視四海，振服群黎。
units.en: 〈Sun Sheng remarks that honoring wise men anchors government; repairing graves marked sage-king usage—only transcendent virtue should command the four seas.
units.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: Honoring worthies and exalting virtue is the vital path of state; tending tombs and marking lanes are august precedents—therefore one must embody heroic breadth and righteousness towering above the age before swaying the realm and awing the multitude.

units.zh: 苟非其人，道不虛行。
units.en: Without the right person principle rings hollow.
units.literal: If the man does not match, the Way walks empty.

units.zh: 靖處室則友於不穆，出身則受位非所，語信則夷險易心，論識則殆為釁首，安在其可寵先而有以感致者乎？
units.en: At home Xu Jing failed brotherly harmony; in career he took ill-fitting posts; in loyal speech he veered with fortune; in counsel he nearly sparked disaster—what merit earns awe?
units.literal: Xu Jing was no harmonious brother at home; in office he held posts unsuited to him; in speech he shifted heart between safety and peril; in judgment he nearly became the cause of strife—wherein lies favor that moves others?

units.zh: 若乃浮虛是崇，偷薄斯榮，則秉直仗義之士，將何以禮之？
units.en: If puffery wins crowns, how do we salute those who stand on integrity?
units.literal: If hollow fame is honored and petty vanity crowned, how shall straight men who cling to duty be treated?

units.zh: 正務眩惑之術，違貴尚之風，譬之郭隗，非其倫矣。
units.en: Fa Zheng used dazzlers’ tricks against noble taste—he is no Guo Wei.
units.literal: Zheng pursued dazzlement’s trick and violated noble fashion—compare him to Guo Wei and he is no peer.

units.zh: 臣松之以為郭隗非賢，猶以權計蒙寵，況文休名聲夙著，天下謂之英偉，雖末年有瑕，而事不彰徹，若不加禮，何以釋遠近之惑乎？
units.en: Pei Songzhi answers: Guo Wei was mediocre yet duped a throne; Xu Jing’s name towered—ignore courtesy and you fuel rumor.
units.literal: Pei Songzhi considers: Guo Wei was no sage yet won favor by stratagem—how much more Xu Jing, whose fame long marked him heroic among the realm; though flawed in old age the faults stayed hidden—without courtesy how quiet distant doubts?

units.zh: 法正以靖方隗，未為不當，而盛以封墓式閭為難，何其迂哉！
units.en: Fa Zheng’s analogy holds; Sun Sheng’s fuss over grave ritual is fussy pedantry.
units.literal: For Fa Zheng to pair Xu Jing with Guo Wei was not wrong—yet Sun Sheng treats tending tombs as scandal—how pedantic!

units.zh: 然則燕昭亦非，豈唯劉翁？
units.en: If so, King Zhao erred too—not Liu Bei alone.
units.literal: Then King Zhao was also wrong—not only “Lord Liu.”

units.zh: 至於友於不穆，失由子將，尋蔣濟之論，知非文休之尤。
units.en: Domestic discord traces to Xu Shao’s verdict—read Jiang Ji and Xu Jing’s guilt shrinks.
units.literal: As for unhappy brotherhood, blame falls on Zijiang—refer to Jiang Ji’s essay and see Xu Jing was hardly chief culprit.

units.zh: 盛又譏其受
units.en: Sun Sheng also ridiculed Xu Jing’s acceptance of
units.literal: Sun Sheng further mocked his accepting

units.en: office—
units.literal: (appointment)

units.zh: 非所，將謂仕於董卓。
units.en: implying he served Dong Zhuo.
units.literal: to mean serving Dong Zhuo.

units.zh: 卓初秉政，顯擢賢俊，受其策爵者森然皆是。
units.en: When Zhuo seized government he promoted talent widely—those who accepted titles were legion.
units.literal: When Zhuo first seized power he elevated worthies wholesale—those who took his patents filled the rolls.

units.zh: 文休為選官。
units.en: Xu Jing directed appointments.
units.literal: Xu Jing served as selection officer.

units.zh: 在卓未至之前，後遷中丞，不為超越。
units.en: That predated Zhuo’s arrival in Luoyang; his promotion to imperial secretary followed normal course.
units.literal: That was before Zhuo reached the capital; later he rose to Palace Assistant Clerk—no leap beyond merit.

units.zh: 以此為貶，則荀爽、陳紀之儔皆應擯棄於世矣。〉
units.en: Condemn him on this ground and you must exile Xun Shuang and Chen Ji as well.
units.literal: To fault him on this would banish Xun Shuang and Chen Ji’s ilk from the age.

units.zh: 以正為蜀郡太守、揚武將軍，外統都畿，內為謀主。
units.en: Fa Zheng became prefect of Shu and General Who Displays Might—he governed the capital region on the outside and framed strategy at Liu Bei’s side within.
units.literal: Zheng was appointed Administrator of Shu Commandery and General Who Displays Might—externally he commanded the metropolitan district; internally he was chief strategist.

units.zh: 一餐之德，睚眥之怨，無不報復，擅殺毀傷己者數人。
units.en: He repaid the slightest kindness or grudge—summarily killing several who had wronged him.
units.literal: For a meal’s kindness or a sidelong grudge he spared no repayment—on his own authority he executed several who had injured him.

units.zh: 或謂諸葛亮曰：「法正於蜀郡太縱橫，將軍宜啟主公，抑其威福。」
units.en: Advisers urged Zhuge Liang: “Fa Zheng abuses his prefecture—tell our lord to rein him in.”
units.literal: Someone told Zhuge Liang: “Fa Zheng runs riot in Shu Commandery—you should inform the sovereign and curb his power.”

units.zh: 亮答曰：「主公之在公安也，北畏曹公之強，東憚孫權之逼，近則懼孫夫人生變於肘腋之下；
units.en: Zhuge Liang answered: “When our lord sheltered at Gong’an he dreaded Cao Cao north, Sun Quan east, and Lady Sun plotting beside him;
units.literal: Liang replied: “When the sovereign was at Gong’an he feared Cao Cao’s strength to the north, Sun Quan’s pressure to the east, and Lady Sun brewing trouble at his elbow;

units.zh: 當斯之時，進退狼跋，法孝直為之輔翼，令翻然翱翔，不可復制，如何禁止法正使不得行其意邪！」
units.en: trapped between threats Fa Xiaozhi lent wings—today he vaults free—why choke Fa Zheng’s desires?”
units.literal: in such straits, advancing or retreating like a wolf in brush, Fa Xiaozhi gave him wings—now he soars beyond restraint—why forbid Fa Zheng his will?”

units.zh: 初，孫權以妹妻先主，妹才捷剛猛，有諸兄之風，侍婢百餘人，皆親執刀侍立，先主每入，衷心常凜凜；
units.en: Sun Quan had married his sister to Liu Bei: she was sharp-tempered and fierce like her brothers, and over a hundred maids stood guard with naked blades—each time Liu Bei crossed her threshold his courage nearly failed him.
units.literal: At first Sun Quan gave his younger sister to the Former Lord in marriage; she was capable, quick, fierce, and bold, with the bearing of her elder brothers; more than a hundred maidservants all stood attendance personally bearing swords; whenever the Former Lord entered, his heart always trembled with dread.

units.zh: 亮又知先主雅愛信正，故言如此。
units.en: Zhuge Liang knew how fond Liu Bei was of Fa Zheng—that is why he framed his answer this way.
units.literal: Liang also knew the Former Lord deeply trusted Zheng—hence these words.

units.zh: 〈孫盛曰：夫威福自下，亡家害國之道，刑縱於寵，毀政亂理之源，安可以功臣而極其陵肆，嬖幸而藉其國柄者哉？
units.en: 〈Sun Sheng argues that delegating supreme authority downward destroys dynasties, and indulgent punishment corrupts rule—no merit minister should be allowed unchecked license or favorite lackeys the imperial grip.
units.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: When awe and blessing rise from below it is the path to ruin house and harm state; when punishment runs loose through favor it is the root of wrecking government and disordering principle—how may merit ministers be stretched to utmost arrogance or favored favorites lent the state’s lever?

units.zh: 故顛頡雖勤，不免違命之刑，楊干雖親，猶加亂行之戮，夫豈不愛，王憲故也。
units.en: Thus Dian Xian earned execution despite diligence; Yang Gan died though royal kin—law, not affection, ruled the realm.
units.literal: Hence though Dian Xian was diligent he did not escape sentence for disobeying orders; though Yang Gan was kin he still suffered execution for unruly conduct—not from lack of love, but because of royal law.

units.zh: 諸葛氏之言，於是乎失政刑矣。〉
units.en: In Sun Sheng’s eyes Zhuge Liang’s defense blurred the line between policy and penal justice.〉
units.literal: Zhuge Liang’s words thus missed balance between governance and punishment.〉

units.zh: 二十二年，正說先主曰：「曹操一舉而降張魯，定漢中，不因此勢以圖巴、蜀，而留夏侯淵、張郃屯守，身遽北還，此非其智不逮而力不足也，必將內有憂偪故耳。
units.en: In 217 Fa Zheng told Liu Bei: “Cao Cao crushed Zhang Lu and took Hanzhong but did not push into Ba–Shu—only Yuan and He remain while he races north; either crisis grips his rear or he lacks nerve.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year Zheng urged the Former Lord: “Cao Cao in one stroke subdued Zhang Lu and secured Hanzhong—yet he did not ride this tide to seize Ba and Shu but left Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He to garrison while he himself hurried north; this is not because his wisdom fell short or strength failed—there must be urgent troubles within.

units.zh: 今策淵、郃才略，不勝國之將帥，舉眾往討，則必可克。
units.en: Yuan and He are no better than our generals—commit the host and you will break them.
units.literal: Now weighed against Yuan and He’s talents and stratagems they do not surpass our state’s commanders—raise the army and attack and victory is assured.

units.zh: 之克克之之日，廣農積谷，觀釁伺隙，上可以傾覆寇敵，尊獎王室，中可以蠶食雍、涼，廣拓境土，下可以固守要害，為持久之計。
units.en: Once Hanzhong falls, farm it, fill granaries, watch for gaps—best case you topple Cao and uphold the Han; mid case you bite into Yong and Liang; worst case you lock the choke points for a long defense.
units.literal: On the day it is taken, expand farming and stockpile grain, watch for openings and wait for cracks—at the summit you may overturn the enemy and exalt the royal house; in the middle you may gnaw Yong and Liang and widen your borders; at the least you may hold vital passes for a war of endurance.

units.zh: 此蓋天以與我，時不可失也。」
units.en: Heaven hands us this opening—we dare not miss it.”
units.literal: This is Heaven’s gift to us—the hour must not slip.”

units.zh: 先主善其策，乃率諸將進兵漢中，正亦從行。
units.en: Liu Bei adopted the plan, advanced on Hanzhong with his commanders, and Fa Zheng rode at his side.
units.literal: The Former Lord approved the stratagem, led the generals toward Hanzhong, and Zheng marched with him.

units.zh: 二十四年，先主自陽平南渡沔水，緣山稍前，於定軍、興勢作營。
units.en: In 219 Liu Bei forded the Han southward from Yangping, hugged the ridges, and camped at Dingjun and Xingshi.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Former Lord crossed the Han south from Yangping, skirted the hills forward, and entrenched at Dingjun and Xingshi.

units.zh: 淵將兵來爭其地。
units.en: Xiahou Yuan moved up to dispute the ground.
units.literal: Yuan led troops to contest the position.

units.zh: 正曰：「可擊矣。」
units.en: Fa Zheng said, “The moment to attack has come.”
units.literal: Zheng said: “We may strike.”

units.zh: 先主命黃忠乘高鼓譟攻之，大破淵軍，淵等授首。
units.en: Liu Bei told Huang Zhong to hold the high ground, drum and clamor, and charge—Yuan’s line shattered and Yuan himself fell.
units.literal: The Former Lord ordered Huang Zhong to seize the heights, beat drums and shout, and attack—utterly defeating Yuan’s army; Yuan and others lost their heads.

units.zh: 曹公西征，聞正之策，曰：「吾故知玄德不辦有此，必為人所教也。」
units.en: Hearing the plan, Cao Cao sneered, “I knew Liu Bei could not think this up alone—some adviser fed him.”
units.literal: The Duke of Cao campaigned west, heard of Zheng’s strategy, and said: “I knew Xuande could not have fashioned this—someone instructed him.”

units.zh: 〈臣松之以為蜀與漢中，其由脣齒也。
units.en: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that Shu and Hanzhong fit together like lip and teeth.
units.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi considers: Shu and Hanzhong are lip and teeth to each other.

units.zh: 劉主之智，豈不及此？
units.en: Did Liu Bei lack wit to see that?
units.literal: Could Lord Liu’s wisdom fail to reach this?

units.zh: 將計略未展，正先發之耳。
units.en: The larger scheme was still forming—Fa Zheng simply voiced it ahead of others.
units.literal: His grand designs had not yet been deployed—Zheng merely spoke first.

units.zh: 夫聽用嘉謀以成功業，霸王之主，誰不皆然？
units.en: What conquering founder ever refused sound advice?
units.literal: Which hegemon who listens to wise counsel to build an empire does not act thus?

units.zh: 魏武以為人所教，亦豈劣哉！
units.en: Even if someone else had advised him, as Emperor Wu of Wei believed, would that make him any less capable?
units.literal: That Cao of Wei thought him coached shows wounded pride, not poor judgment.

units.zh: 此蓋恥恨之餘辭，非測實之當言也。〉
units.en: Those were merely bitter words born of wounded pride, not a fair assessment of the facts.〉
units.literal: This is bitter language left over from shame, not measured speech that fits the facts.〉

units.zh: 先主立為漢中王，以正為尚書令、護軍將軍。
units.en: As King of Hanzhong Liu Bei named Fa Zheng Director of the Secretariat and General Who Guards the Army.
units.literal: When the Former Lord was invested King of Hanzhong he appointed Zheng Director of the Secretariat and General Who Protects the Army.

units.zh: 明年卒，時年四十五。
units.en: He died the following year at forty-five.
units.literal: He died the next year at forty-five.

units.zh: 先主為之流涕者累日。
units.en: Liu Bei mourned him day after day.
units.literal: The Former Lord wept for him for days on end.

units.zh: 諡曰翼侯。
units.en: His posthumous name was Marquis Yi (“Wing”).
units.literal: Posthumous title Marquis Yi.

units.zh: 賜子邈爵關內侯，官至奉車都尉、漢陽太守。
units.en: His son Miao was granted the rank of Marquis Within the Passes and rose to become Colonel of the Chariots and Administrator of Hanyang.
units.literal: His son Miao was granted rank as Marquis Within the Passes and rose to Colonel Director of Retinue and Administrator of Hanyang.

units.zh: 諸葛亮與正，雖好尚不同，以公義相取。
units.en: Though Zhuge Liang and Fa Zheng differed in their tastes and values, they respected each other’s commitment to the public good.
units.literal: Though Zhuge Liang and Zheng differed in inclinations, they chose each other by public duty.

units.zh: 亮每奇正智術。
units.en: Zhuge Liang repeatedly admired Fa Zheng’s schemes.
units.literal: Liang always marveled at Zheng’s stratagems.

units.zh: 先主既即尊號，將東征孫權以復關羽之恥，群臣多諫，一不從。
units.en: Once Liu Bei took the throne, he prepared to march east against Sun Quan and avenge the humiliation of Guan Yu’s defeat; his ministers repeatedly remonstrated, but he ignored them all.
units.literal: After the Former Lord assumed the imperial title he prepared to march east against Sun Quan to avenge Guan Yu’s shame—many ministers remonstrated and none were heeded.

units.zh: 章武二年，大軍敗績，還住白帝。
units.en: In Zhangwu 2 the host was shattered and Liu Bei fell back to Baidi.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhangwu the great army suffered defeat and withdrew to Baidi.

units.zh: 亮嘆曰：「法孝直若在，則能制主上，令不東行；
units.en: Zhuge Liang sighed, “Had Fa Zheng lived he could have checked our lord and blocked the eastern march;
units.literal: Liang sighed: “If Fa Xiaozhi lived he could restrain the sovereign and keep him from marching east;

units.zh: 就復東行，必不傾危矣。」
units.en: even forced eastward, we might not have faced catastrophe.”
units.literal: even had he marched east, ruin would not have followed.”

units.zh: 〈先主與曹公爭，勢有不便，宜退，而先主大怒不肯退，無敢諫者。
units.en: 〈Once, opposing Cao Cao, Liu Bei ought to have retreated but raged and stayed—no one dared speak.
units.literal: 〈When the Former Lord contended with the Duke of Cao and the situation turned disadvantageous so withdrawal was fitting, the Former Lord grew furious and refused to withdraw—none dared remonstrate.

units.zh: 矢下如雨，正乃往當先主前，先主雲：「孝直避箭。」
units.en: Shafts filled the sky; Fa Zheng planted himself in front until Liu Bei cried, “Xiaozhi—take cover!”
units.literal: Arrows fell like rain; Zheng went and stood before the Former Lord; the Former Lord said: “Xiaozhi, dodge the arrows.”

units.zh: 正曰：「明公親當矢石，況小人乎？」
units.en: Fa Zheng answered, “If you brave bolts and stone, how can I shrink back?”
units.literal: Zheng said: “When my Brilliant Lord himself faces arrows and stones, how much more a petty man like me?”

units.zh: 先主乃曰：「孝直，吾與汝俱去。」
units.en: Liu Bei said, “Xiaozhi—then we retreat together.”
units.literal: The Former Lord then said: “Xiaozhi, I withdraw with you.”

units.zh: 遂退。〉
units.en: They broke off and withdrew.〉
units.literal: Thereupon they withdrew.〉

units.en: Editorial heading: Appraisal.
units.literal: 【Appraisal】

units.zh: 評曰：龐統雅好人流，經學思謀，于時荊﹑楚謂之高俊．法正著見成敗，有奇畫策算，然不以德素稱也．儗之魏臣，統其荀彧之仲叔，正其程﹑郭之儔儷邪？
units.en: The historian concludes: Pang Tong cultivated talent and strategic thought—southerners called him eminent. Fa Zheng read victory and defeat with uncanny plans yet lacked renown for steady morals. Against Wei’s councilors, Tong rivals Xun Yu; Zheng belongs with Cheng Yu and Guo Jia.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Pang Tong loved to survey men and ponder classical learning and strategy—among Jing and Chu of the time he was deemed lofty. Fa Zheng saw success and failure clearly and devised singular stratagems, yet was not famed for constant virtue. Set beside Wei ministers, is Tong the peer of Xun Yu, and Zheng the companion of Cheng Yu and Guo Jia?
